panels.visual: Plato in an olive grove handing two modern girls sticks to draw in the sand
panels.caption: I am Plato. Draw me a perfect circle.

panels.visual: The girls' circles in the sand, Plato peering at them with a magnifying lens showing bumps and wobbles
panels.caption: However carefully you draw, every circle is a little wobbly.

panels.visual: Plato tapping his head with a glowing perfect circle above it
panels.caption: Yet you know exactly what a perfect circle is. So where is it?

panels.visual: A bright upper world of glowing perfect shapes, and below it our world of objects as their shadows
panels.caption: Plato said perfect things, the Forms, are real but not in this world. Everything we see is a shadow of them.

panels.visual: Prisoners chained in a dark cave staring at shadows on a wall, cast by a fire behind them and puppets carried past
panels.caption: He told a story: prisoners chained in a cave, watching shadows on a wall, think the shadows are real.

panels.visual: One prisoner escaping up a tunnel into dazzling sunlight, seeing trees and the sun for the first time
panels.caption: One escapes into the sunlight and sees real things for the first time.

panels.visual: He goes back down into the cave to tell the others, and they laugh and jeer at him
panels.caption: He goes back to tell the others. They laugh at him.

panels.visual: Plato and Glauka the owl with a geometry drawing of a triangle and circle
panels.caption: That's why Plato loved geometry: it trains your mind to see past the shadows.
